title: Mi familia
text:
Hola. Me llamo Camila. Tengo veinte años. Vivo en Bogotá con mi familia. Vivimos en un apartamento.

Mi papá se llama Ricardo. Es profesor. Mi mamá se llama Patricia. Es enfermera. Tengo un hermano. Se llama Sebastián. Tiene quince años. Él estudia en el colegio. Yo estudio en la universidad.

Mi abuela Inés también vive con nosotros. Ella cocina muy bien. Tenemos un perro. Se llama Coco. Es pequeño y blanco. ¡Quiero mucho a mi familia!
translation:
Hi. My name is Camila. I'm twenty years old. I live in Bogotá with my family. We live in an apartment.

My dad's name is Ricardo. He's a teacher. My mom's name is Patricia. She's a nurse. I have a brother. His name is Sebastián. He's fifteen. He goes to school. I study at the university.

My grandmother Inés also lives with us. She cooks very well. We have a dog. His name is Coco. He's small and white. I love my family very much!

questions.q: What is the text about?
questions.explain: Camila introduces herself and describes her dad, mom, brother, grandmother and dog.

questions.q: What does Camila's father do?
questions.explain: The text says 'Mi papá se llama Ricardo. Es profesor.'

questions.q: How many people live in the apartment?
questions.explain: Camila, her dad, her mom, her brother and her grandmother ('también vive con nosotros') make five people; Coco is a dog.

title: La tienda de don Pacho
text:
TIENDA DON PACHO
Calle 45 # 13-20
¡Abierto todos los días!

Horario:
Lunes a viernes: 6:00 a. m. a 9:00 p. m.
Sábados: 7:00 a. m. a 9:00 p. m.
Domingos y festivos: 8:00 a. m. a 1:00 p. m.

Hay pan, leche, huevos, queso y arepas. También hay frutas, verduras, café y jugos. ¡El pan es fresco todos los días!
Pago en efectivo o con tarjeta.
Hay domicilios en el barrio. El domicilio es gratis.
Teléfono: 312 555 7781
translation:
DON PACHO'S SHOP
Calle 45 # 13-20
Open every day!

Opening hours:
Monday to Friday: 6:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m.
Saturdays: 7:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m.
Sundays and public holidays: 8:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m.

We have bread, milk, eggs, cheese and arepas. We also have fruit, vegetables, coffee and juices. The bread is fresh every day!
Payment in cash or by card.
Home delivery in the neighborhood. Delivery is free.
Phone: 312 555 7781

questions.q: What is this notice for?
options: To find a new worker for the shop
To show a shop's hours and products
To invite people to a party at the shop
To say that the shop is closing
questions.explain: The notice gives the 'Horario' for each day and lists what the shop sells: 'Hay pan, leche, huevos…'.

questions.q: What time does the shop open on Saturdays?
questions.explain: The notice says 'Sábados: 7:00 a. m. a 9:00 p. m.'

questions.q: It is Sunday at 3:00 p.m. Can you buy bread at the shop?
options: No, the shop is closed then.
Yes, but only with a card.
Yes, the shop closes at 9:00 p.m.
Yes, there is fresh bread every day.
questions.explain: On Sundays the shop is open '8:00 a. m. a 1:00 p. m.', so at 3:00 p.m. it is closed.

topic: meeting a friend at a café
title: ¿Dónde estás?
text:
Valeria: Hola, Santi. ¿Dónde estás? Yo estoy en el café. Es el café de la calle 53, al lado del parque. Estoy en una mesa cerca de la ventana. Tengo una chaqueta roja.
Valeria: El café es muy bonito. Hay tinto, jugos y pan de bono. ¿Llegas pronto?
Santiago: ¡Hola, Vale! Qué pena. Estoy en el bus. Hay mucho tráfico. Llego en veinte minutos.
Santiago: ¿Pides un tinto para mí, por favor?
Valeria: Listo. Te espero.
translation:
Valeria: Hi, Santi. Where are you? I'm at the café. It's the café on Calle 53, next to the park. I'm at a table near the window. I'm wearing a red jacket.
Valeria: The café is really nice. There's tinto (black coffee), juices and pan de bono. Will you be here soon?
Santiago: Hi, Vale! I'm so sorry. I'm on the bus. There's a lot of traffic. I'll be there in twenty minutes.
Santiago: Can you order a tinto for me, please?
Valeria: Sure. I'll wait for you.

questions.q: Why does Valeria write to Santiago?
options: To ask him for some money
To invite him to her house
To say she is on the bus
To tell him where she is
questions.explain: Valeria writes 'Yo estoy en el café… cerca de la ventana' so that Santiago can find her.

questions.q: Why is Santiago late?
options: There is a lot of traffic.
questions.explain: Santiago writes 'Estoy en el bus. Hay mucho tráfico.'

questions.q: What does Santiago mean by 'Qué pena'?
questions.explain: He says 'Qué pena' right before explaining that he is late, so it is an apology: 'I'm sorry'.

topic: Sunday bike ride at the ciclovía
title: Domingo de ciclovía
text:
Hoy es domingo. Natalia y su papá van a la ciclovía. Los domingos, muchas calles de Bogotá no tienen carros. Son para las bicicletas y las personas.

Natalia tiene una bicicleta azul. Su papá tiene una bicicleta verde. En la calle hay mucha gente. Unos montan en bicicleta. Otros caminan o corren. También hay perros.

A las once, Natalia tiene sed. Ella y su papá toman jugo de naranja. Natalia está muy feliz. “¡Me encanta mi cicla!”, dice.
translation:
Today is Sunday. Natalia and her dad are going to the ciclovía. On Sundays, many streets in Bogotá have no cars. They are for bicycles and people.

Natalia has a blue bicycle. Her dad has a green bicycle. There are a lot of people in the street. Some ride bikes. Others walk or run. There are also dogs.

At eleven, Natalia is thirsty. She and her dad have orange juice. Natalia is very happy. “I love my bike!” she says.

questions.q: What is the text about?
options: A race for children and dogs
questions.explain: Natalia and her dad go to the 'ciclovía' on Sunday, when many streets of Bogotá 'no tienen carros'.

questions.q: What do Natalia and her dad drink at eleven?
questions.explain: At eleven Natalia is thirsty ('tiene sed'), and they drink 'jugo de naranja'.

questions.q: Natalia says '¡Me encanta mi cicla!' What is a 'cicla'?
questions.explain: Natalia rides 'una bicicleta azul' and then talks about 'mi cicla', so 'cicla' is a Colombian word for bicycle.

title: La vecina nueva
text:
—Buenos días. ¿Usted es la vecina nueva?
—Sí, señor. Me llamo Carolina. Vivo en el 302.
—Mucho gusto, Carolina. Yo soy Hernán. Vivo en el 301, al lado.
—Mucho gusto, don Hernán.
—¿Usted vive sola?
—No, vivo con mi hija. Ella tiene seis años.
—¡Qué bien! Yo vivo con mi esposa y un perro. El perro se llama Toby. Es grande, pero es muy tranquilo.
—¡A mi hija le encantan los perros!
—Entonces Toby tiene una amiga nueva. Bienvenidas al edificio.
translation:
—Good morning. Are you the new neighbor?
—Yes, sir. My name is Carolina. I live in 302.
—Nice to meet you, Carolina. I'm Hernán. I live in 301, next door.
—Nice to meet you, Don Hernán.
—Do you live alone?
—No, I live with my daughter. She's six years old.
—How nice! I live with my wife and a dog. The dog's name is Toby. He's big, but he's very calm.
—My daughter loves dogs!
—Then Toby has a new friend. Welcome to the building, both of you.

questions.q: What is happening in the dialogue?
options: A woman looks for her dog
questions.explain: Hernán asks '¿Usted es la vecina nueva?' and they introduce themselves with 'Mucho gusto'.

questions.q: Who does Carolina live with?
questions.explain: Carolina says 'vivo con mi hija. Ella tiene seis años.'

questions.q: Hernán lives in 301, 'al lado'. What does 'al lado' mean?
questions.explain: Carolina lives in 302 and Hernán in 301, on the same floor, so 'al lado' means next door.

title: Frío y lluvia en Bogotá
text:
Juliana vive en Bogotá. Bogotá está en las montañas. Por eso, el clima es frío. Por la mañana, hace mucho frío. Al mediodía, a veces hace sol. Por la tarde, muchas veces llueve.

Juliana siempre lleva una chaqueta y una sombrilla en el bolso. Pero hoy no tiene sombrilla. ¡La sombrilla está en la casa!

A las cuatro, llueve mucho. Juliana espera en una cafetería. Toma una aromática caliente. A las cinco, ya no llueve. Juliana camina a la casa.
translation:
Juliana lives in Bogotá. Bogotá is in the mountains. That's why the climate is cold. In the morning, it's very cold. At noon, it's sometimes sunny. In the afternoon, it often rains.

Juliana always carries a jacket and an umbrella in her bag. But today she doesn't have an umbrella. The umbrella is at home!

At four o'clock, it rains a lot. Juliana waits in a café. She has a hot herbal tea. At five, it isn't raining anymore. Juliana walks home.

questions.q: What is the text mainly about?
options: A trip to the mountains near Bogotá
How to make a hot herbal tea
A new café in downtown Bogotá
questions.explain: The text describes the weather in Bogotá ('hace mucho frío… muchas veces llueve') and Juliana's rainy afternoon.

questions.q: What does Juliana do when it rains a lot?
questions.explain: The text says 'A las cuatro, llueve mucho. Juliana espera en una cafetería.'

questions.q: What is a 'sombrilla'?
questions.explain: Juliana carries it for the rain, and without it she has to wait in a café while 'llueve mucho': it is an umbrella.

title: Se arrienda apartamento
text:
SE ARRIENDA APARTAMENTO EN CHAPINERO, BOGOTÁ

Bonito apartamento en el tercer piso. Tiene dos habitaciones, un baño, una cocina y una sala grande. La sala tiene mucha luz. El edificio no tiene ascensor, pero tiene portería las 24 horas.

Cerca hay un parque, un supermercado y un paradero de bus. El barrio es tranquilo. Precio: $1.400.000 al mes. No se aceptan mascotas.
Información: Gloria Rincón, 316 555 2048 (llamar de lunes a sábado).
translation:
APARTMENT FOR RENT IN CHAPINERO, BOGOTÁ

Nice apartment on the third floor. It has two bedrooms, one bathroom, a kitchen and a big living room. The living room gets a lot of light. The building has no elevator, but it has a 24-hour doorman.

Nearby there is a park, a supermarket and a bus stop. The neighborhood is quiet. Price: 1,400,000 pesos a month. No pets allowed.
Information: Gloria Rincón, 316 555 2048 (call Monday to Saturday).

questions.q: What does this advert offer?
questions.explain: The heading says 'SE ARRIENDA APARTAMENTO' (apartment for rent), and the advert gives a price 'al mes'.

questions.q: What floor is the apartment on?
questions.explain: The advert says 'Bonito apartamento en el tercer piso.'

questions.q: Who CANNOT rent this apartment?
questions.explain: The advert says 'No se aceptan mascotas' (no pets allowed), so a woman with two cats cannot rent it.

title: El almuerzo del día
text:
—Buenas tardes. ¿Qué hay de almuerzo hoy?
—Hoy hay sopa de verduras. De seco, hay pollo o carne. Los dos vienen con arroz, papa y ensalada.
—¿Y qué jugo hay?
—Hay jugo de mora o de guanábana.
—Pollo y jugo de mora, por favor. ¿Cuánto vale el almuerzo?
—Vale quince mil pesos. El postre está incluido.
—¡Qué bien! ¿Y qué postre hay?
—Hoy hay arroz con leche.
—Perfecto. ¿Me regala un vaso de agua, por favor?
—Con mucho gusto.
translation:
—Good afternoon. What's for lunch today?
—Today there's vegetable soup. For the main course, there's chicken or beef. Both come with rice, potatoes and salad.
—And what juice is there?
—There's blackberry or soursop juice.
—Chicken and blackberry juice, please. How much is the lunch?
—It's fifteen thousand pesos. Dessert is included.
—Great! And what's for dessert?
—Today there's rice pudding.
—Perfect. Could I have a glass of water, please?
—My pleasure.

questions.q: Where does this conversation happen?
questions.explain: A customer asks '¿Qué hay de almuerzo hoy?' and orders soup, a main dish, juice and dessert, as in a restaurant.

questions.q: How much does the lunch cost?
questions.explain: The waiter says 'Vale quince mil pesos. El postre está incluido.'

questions.q: On this menu, what is the 'seco'?
questions.explain: After the soup comes 'De seco, hay pollo o carne' with rice, potatoes and salad, so the 'seco' is the main dish.

title: ¿Puedes ir a la tienda?
titleEn: Can You Go to the Shop?
text:
Hola, Esteban. Hoy llego tarde a la casa, a las nueve de la noche. ¡Y en la nevera no hay nada! ¿Puedes ir a la tienda de la esquina, por favor? Necesitamos:
- una docena de huevos
- una libra de arroz
- dos bolsas de leche
- un pan tajado
- tomates y cebolla

La plata está en el cajón de la cocina. Son cincuenta mil pesos. Mañana yo cocino arroz con huevo para los dos. ¡Gracias, parce!
Diego
translation:
Hi, Esteban. I'm getting home late today, at nine at night. And there's nothing in the fridge! Can you go to the corner shop, please? We need:
- a dozen eggs
- a pound of rice
- two bags of milk
- a loaf of sliced bread
- tomatoes and onion

The money is in the kitchen drawer. It's fifty thousand pesos. Tomorrow I'll cook rice with egg for both of us. Thanks, buddy!
Diego

questions.q: Why does Diego write to Esteban?
options: To invite him to dinner tonight
To ask him for fifty thousand pesos
To ask him to buy some food
To say the fridge is broken
questions.explain: Diego asks '¿Puedes ir a la tienda de la esquina, por favor?' and lists what they need.

questions.q: What time does Diego get home today?
questions.explain: Diego writes 'Hoy llego tarde a la casa, a las nueve de la noche.'

questions.q: Diego writes 'La plata está en el cajón'. What is 'plata' here?
questions.explain: Right after it, Diego writes 'Son cincuenta mil pesos', so 'plata' is an informal Colombian word for money.

title: Clases de español
text:
Asunto: Clases de español
Buenos días:
Me llamo Sarah Miller. Soy de Canadá y vivo en Bogotá desde enero. Trabajo en una empresa de turismo. Hablo un poco de español, pero quiero aprender más. Por eso, quiero estudiar en su escuela.

Tengo unas preguntas. ¿Tienen clases por la noche? Trabajo de lunes a viernes, de ocho a cinco. ¿Cuántos estudiantes hay en cada clase? ¿Cuánto cuesta un curso de un mes?

Muchas gracias.
Saludos,
Sarah
translation:
Subject: Spanish classes
Good morning,
My name is Sarah Miller. I'm from Canada and I've lived in Bogotá since January. I work for a tourism company. I speak a little Spanish, but I want to learn more. That's why I want to study at your school.

I have a few questions. Do you have evening classes? I work Monday to Friday, from eight to five. How many students are there in each class? How much does a one-month course cost?

Thank you very much.
Best regards,
Sarah

questions.q: Why does Sarah write this email?
options: To find a job in a school
To invite a teacher to Canada
To book a trip to Bogotá
questions.explain: Sarah writes 'quiero estudiar en su escuela' and asks about the classes, the students and the price.

questions.q: Where is Sarah from?
questions.explain: Sarah writes 'Soy de Canadá y vivo en Bogotá desde enero.'

questions.q: Why does Sarah ask about evening classes?
options: She has classes in the morning.
questions.explain: She writes 'Trabajo de lunes a viernes, de ocho a cinco', so she is only free in the evening.

title: ¿Dónde están las llaves?
text:
Son las siete y media. Julián sale para el trabajo. Pero hay un problema: ¡no encuentra las llaves!

Busca en la mesa de la sala. No están. Busca en la cocina, al lado de la nevera. Tampoco están. Busca en el baño y en el cuarto. Nada. Entonces, llama a su esposa, Mónica.
—Mónica, ¿dónde están mis llaves?
Mónica se ríe.
—Julián, están en el bolsillo de tu chaqueta.

Julián mira. ¡Es verdad! Ya son las ocho. Hoy llega tarde al trabajo.
translation:
It's half past seven. Julián is leaving for work. But there's a problem: he can't find his keys!

He looks on the living room table. They aren't there. He looks in the kitchen, next to the fridge. They aren't there either. He looks in the bathroom and in the bedroom. Nothing. Then he calls his wife, Mónica.
“Mónica, where are my keys?”
Mónica laughs.
“Julián, they're in your jacket pocket.”

Julián looks. It's true! It's already eight o'clock. Today he's late for work.

questions.q: What is the problem in the story?
questions.explain: The text says 'hay un problema: ¡no encuentra las llaves!'

questions.q: Where are the keys?
questions.explain: Mónica says 'están en el bolsillo de tu chaqueta', and Julián sees it is true.

questions.q: Why is Julián late for work today?
options: He wakes up at eight o'clock.
He has a long breakfast with Mónica.
He spends time looking for his keys.
questions.explain: He is ready to leave at 'las siete y media', searches the whole house, and when he finds the keys 'Ya son las ocho'.

title: En la droguería
text:
—Buenas tardes. ¿En qué le puedo ayudar?
—Buenas tardes. Tengo dolor de cabeza y un poco de fiebre.
—¿Desde cuándo?
—Desde anoche.
—¿Tiene tos o dolor de garganta?
—No, solo dolor de cabeza y fiebre.
—Bueno, puede tomar acetaminofén. Es una pastilla cada ocho horas, con agua.
—¿Cuánto vale la caja?
—Seis mil pesos.
—Listo, aquí tiene.
—Gracias. También tiene que descansar y tomar mucho líquido. Si mañana todavía tiene fiebre, debe ir al médico.
—Muchas gracias, muy amable.
translation:
—Good afternoon. How can I help you?
—Good afternoon. I have a headache and a bit of a fever.
—Since when?
—Since last night.
—Do you have a cough or a sore throat?
—No, just a headache and a fever.
—OK, you can take acetaminophen. It's one pill every eight hours, with water.
—How much is the box?
—Six thousand pesos.
—OK, here you go.
—Thank you. You also need to rest and drink plenty of fluids. If you still have a fever tomorrow, you should go to the doctor.
—Thank you very much, that's very kind of you.

questions.q: What is happening in the dialogue?
options: A doctor visits a sick child
A man buys food for dinner
Two friends talk about a trip
questions.explain: The customer says 'Tengo dolor de cabeza y un poco de fiebre' and buys a box of acetaminofén.

questions.q: How often should the customer take the medicine?
questions.explain: The pharmacist says 'Es una pastilla cada ocho horas, con agua.'

questions.q: What is a 'pastilla'?
questions.explain: The customer must take acetaminofén, 'una pastilla cada ocho horas, con agua', and buys a box of them: a 'pastilla' is a pill.

title: Un domicilio
text:
Es viernes. Catalina llega a la casa a las ocho de la noche. Está muy cansada y tiene hambre. No quiere cocinar. Entonces, abre una aplicación en el celular. Pide un domicilio: una pizza y una limonada. La aplicación dice: “Su pedido llega en treinta minutos”.

Catalina se baña y se pone la pijama. A las ocho y media, suena el celular. Es el portero del edificio:
—Señora Catalina, aquí hay un domiciliario con un pedido para usted.
—¡Gracias, ya bajo!
translation:
It's Friday. Catalina gets home at eight in the evening. She's very tired and hungry. She doesn't want to cook. So she opens an app on her phone. She orders a delivery: a pizza and a lemonade. The app says: “Your order will arrive in thirty minutes.”

Catalina takes a shower and puts on her pajamas. At half past eight, her phone rings. It's the building's doorman:
“Ms. Catalina, there's a delivery man here with an order for you.”
“Thanks, I'm coming down!”

questions.q: What is the story about?
options: Catalina cooks a pizza at home
Catalina orders food on an app
Catalina eats at a pizza restaurant
questions.explain: Catalina 'No quiere cocinar', so she opens 'una aplicación en el celular' and 'Pide un domicilio: una pizza y una limonada'.

questions.q: Who calls Catalina at half past eight?
questions.explain: The text says 'suena el celular. Es el portero del edificio'.

questions.q: What is a 'domiciliario'?
questions.explain: The doorman says the 'domiciliario' is there 'con un pedido para usted' (with an order for you), so he is the delivery person.

title: Hoy no puedo ir
text:
Asunto: Hoy no puedo ir
Hola, Diana:
Buenos días. Hoy no puedo ir a la oficina porque estoy enfermo. Tengo fiebre y me duele mucho la garganta. A las diez tengo cita con el médico.

La reunión con los clientes es hoy a las tres. ¿Puede Camilo presentar el informe? El documento está en la carpeta “Ventas”, en el computador de la oficina. Mañana le escribo otra vez.

Muchas gracias y disculpe.
Sergio
translation:
Subject: I can't come in today
Hi Diana,
Good morning. I can't come to the office today because I'm sick. I have a fever and my throat really hurts. I have a doctor's appointment at ten.

The meeting with the clients is today at three. Can Camilo present the report? The document is in the “Ventas” (Sales) folder, on the office computer. I'll write to you again tomorrow.

Many thanks, and sorry.
Sergio

questions.q: Why does Sergio write to Diana?
options: To invite her to a meeting
To ask for a new computer
To say he is sick today
To ask her to see a doctor
questions.explain: Sergio writes 'Hoy no puedo ir a la oficina porque estoy enfermo.'

questions.q: What time is Sergio's doctor's appointment?
questions.explain: He writes 'A las diez tengo cita con el médico'; three o'clock is the time of the meeting.

questions.q: What is the 'informe' in this email?
questions.explain: Camilo must 'presentar el informe' at the meeting, and Sergio calls it 'El documento' in the 'Ventas' folder.

title: Un viaje largo
text:
Andrea vive en el sur de Bogotá, pero trabaja en el norte. Todos los días sale de la casa a las seis. Primero, camina diez minutos hasta el paradero. Allí, en una tienda, recarga la tarjeta del bus.

El viaje es largo: una hora y media. A esa hora, el bus siempre está lleno y Andrea casi nunca tiene puesto. Va de pie. Escucha música con sus audífonos y lee las noticias en el celular. Llega a la oficina a las ocho.
translation:
Andrea lives in the south of Bogotá, but she works in the north. Every day she leaves home at six. First, she walks ten minutes to the bus stop. There, in a shop, she tops up her bus card.

The trip is long: an hour and a half. At that time, the bus is always full and Andrea almost never gets a seat. She stands. She listens to music on her headphones and reads the news on her phone. She gets to the office at eight.

questions.q: What is the text mainly about?
options: Andrea's new job in the south
A shop that sells bus cards
questions.explain: Andrea lives in the south and works in the north, and 'El viaje es largo: una hora y media.'

questions.q: How long is the bus trip?
questions.explain: The text says 'El viaje es largo: una hora y media.'

questions.q: Andrea 'casi nunca tiene puesto'. What does this mean?
options: She almost never has her card.
She almost never gets a seat.
questions.explain: The bus 'siempre está lleno' and the next words are 'Va de pie' (she stands), so 'puesto' means a seat.

title: La fiesta sorpresa
text:
Luisa: ¡Hola a todos! El sábado es el cumpleaños de Carlos. Cumple treinta años. Vamos a hacer una fiesta sorpresa en mi apartamento, a las siete de la noche. ¿Quién puede venir?
Óscar: ¡Qué chévere! Yo voy. Llevo el ponqué y las velas.
Viviana: Yo también voy, pero trabajo hasta las siete. ¿Está bien a las ocho?
Luisa: Sí, claro. Carlos llega a las ocho y media. ¡Pero es un secreto! Carlos no sabe nada.
Óscar: ¡Perfecto! Nos vemos el sábado.
translation:
Luisa: Hi everyone! Saturday is Carlos's birthday. He's turning thirty. We're going to have a surprise party at my apartment, at seven in the evening. Who can come?
Óscar: How cool! I'm coming. I'll bring the cake and the candles.
Viviana: I'm coming too, but I work until seven. Is eight OK?
Luisa: Yes, of course. Carlos is arriving at half past eight. But it's a secret! Carlos doesn't know anything.
Óscar: Perfect! See you on Saturday.

questions.q: Why does Luisa write to the group?
options: To ask for a birthday gift
To change the date of a party
questions.explain: Luisa writes 'Vamos a hacer una fiesta sorpresa en mi apartamento… ¿Quién puede venir?'

questions.q: Why can't Viviana arrive at seven?
options: She has a class until eight.
questions.explain: Viviana writes 'Yo también voy, pero trabajo hasta las siete.'

questions.q: Óscar writes 'Llevo el ponqué y las velas'. What is a 'ponqué'?
questions.explain: Óscar brings it with 'las velas' (the candles) for a birthday party, so a 'ponqué' is a cake.

topic: recipe for hot chocolate with cheese
title: Chocolate con queso
text:
Chocolate con queso (para dos personas)

Ingredientes: dos tazas de leche, dos pastillas de chocolate y dos pedazos de queso campesino.

1. Calentar la leche en una olla.
2. Agregar el chocolate y esperar cinco minutos.
3. Batir con el molinillo hasta hacer espuma.
4. Servir el chocolate en dos tazas.
5. Poner un pedazo de queso en cada taza y esperar un minuto.
En Bogotá, mucha gente toma este chocolate en las onces, a las cinco de la tarde, con pan.
translation:
Hot chocolate with cheese (for two people)

Ingredients: two cups of milk, two tablets of chocolate and two pieces of farmer's cheese.

1. Heat the milk in a pot.
2. Add the chocolate and wait five minutes.
3. Whisk with the molinillo (a wooden whisk) until it froths.
4. Serve the chocolate in two cups.
5. Put a piece of cheese in each cup and wait one minute.
In Bogotá, many people have this chocolate at 'las onces', at five in the afternoon, with bread.

questions.q: What is this text?
questions.explain: It lists 'Ingredientes' and numbered steps to make hot chocolate: 'Calentar la leche… Agregar el chocolate…'.

questions.q: What do you put in each cup at the end?
questions.explain: Step 5 says 'Poner un pedazo de queso en cada taza y esperar un minuto.'

questions.q: What are 'las onces' in Bogotá?
questions.explain: People have this chocolate 'en las onces, a las cinco de la tarde, con pan', so 'las onces' is an afternoon snack.

title: ¿Hay un cajero por aquí?
titleEn: Is There an ATM Around Here?
text:
—Disculpe, señor. ¿Hay un cajero automático por aquí?
—Sí, hay uno en el centro comercial. Siga derecho por esta calle dos cuadras. En la esquina, voltee a la izquierda. El centro comercial está al frente de un parque.
—¿Y dónde está el cajero?
—En el primer piso, al lado de la entrada.
—¿Está lejos?
—No, son cinco minutos a pie.
—¿El centro comercial abre los domingos?
—Sí, abre todos los días hasta las nueve.
—Muchas gracias, muy amable.
—A la orden.
translation:
—Excuse me, sir. Is there an ATM around here?
—Yes, there's one in the shopping mall. Go straight along this street for two blocks. At the corner, turn left. The shopping mall is across from a park.
—And where is the ATM?
—On the first floor, next to the entrance.
—Is it far?
—No, it's five minutes on foot.
—Does the shopping mall open on Sundays?
—Yes, it's open every day until nine.
—Thank you very much, that's very kind of you.
—You're welcome.

questions.q: What is the first speaker looking for?
questions.explain: The first speaker asks '¿Hay un cajero automático por aquí?'

questions.q: How do you get to the shopping mall?
options: Go straight two blocks, then turn left
Go straight two blocks, then turn right
Go straight one block, then turn left
Turn left, then go straight two blocks
questions.explain: The man says 'Siga derecho por esta calle dos cuadras. En la esquina, voltee a la izquierda.'

questions.q: The man answers 'A la orden'. What does he mean?
questions.explain: He says it right after 'Muchas gracias, muy amable', so 'A la orden' is a polite Colombian way to say 'you're welcome'.

title: Problema con la lavadora
titleEn: A Problem with the Washing Machine
text:
Asunto: Problema con la lavadora
Buenos días, señor Ramírez:
Le escribo porque tengo un problema en el apartamento. La lavadora prende, pero no saca el agua. La ropa siempre queda mojada. Por eso, ahora lavo la ropa a mano.

¿Puede mandar a un técnico esta semana? Estoy en la casa el jueves por la tarde y el sábado por la mañana. Además, tengo una pregunta: ¿quién paga el arreglo, usted o yo?

Muchas gracias.
Cordialmente,
Paula Gómez
Apartamento 501
translation:
Subject: Problem with the washing machine
Good morning, Mr. Ramírez,
I'm writing to you because I have a problem in the apartment. The washing machine turns on, but it doesn't drain the water. The clothes always stay wet. That's why I'm washing my clothes by hand now.

Can you send a technician this week? I'm at home on Thursday afternoon and Saturday morning. Also, I have a question: who pays for the repair, you or me?

Thank you very much.
Kind regards,
Paula Gómez
Apartment 501

questions.q: Why does Paula write to Mr. Ramírez?
options: To ask how to use the washing machine
To report a broken washing machine
To pay the rent for this month
To say she is moving out soon
questions.explain: Paula writes 'tengo un problema en el apartamento. La lavadora prende, pero no saca el agua.'

questions.q: When is Paula at home?
questions.explain: She writes 'Estoy en la casa el jueves por la tarde y el sábado por la mañana.'

questions.q: Paula asks who pays 'el arreglo'. What is 'el arreglo'?
options: The cost of a new machine
questions.explain: Paula asks for 'un técnico' to come and fix the machine, then asks who pays 'el arreglo': the repair.

title: Vacaciones en Salento
text:
Manuela y su novio, Nicolás, están de vacaciones en Salento. Es un pueblo pequeño en la zona cafetera de Colombia. Las casas son blancas, con puertas y balcones de muchos colores.

Por la mañana, visitan una finca de café. Un campesino les muestra las plantas. Después, compran una libra de café para la familia.

Por la tarde, caminan por el valle de Cocora. Allí hay palmas de cera, el árbol nacional de Colombia. ¡Son altísimas! Mañana, van a montar a caballo.
translation:
Manuela and her boyfriend, Nicolás, are on vacation in Salento. It's a small town in Colombia's coffee region. The houses are white, with doors and balconies in many colors.

In the morning, they visit a coffee farm. A farmer shows them the plants. Then they buy a pound of coffee for the family.

In the afternoon, they walk through the Cocora Valley. There are wax palms there, Colombia's national tree. They're extremely tall! Tomorrow, they're going to go horseback riding.

questions.q: What is the text about?
options: A couple's vacation in a small town
A family that sells coffee in Bogotá
A school trip to a big city
Two sisters who live in Bogotá
questions.explain: Manuela and her boyfriend 'están de vacaciones en Salento', 'un pueblo pequeño'.

questions.q: What do Manuela and Nicolás buy for the family?
questions.explain: The text says 'compran una libra de café para la familia.'

questions.q: What is a 'finca' in this text?
questions.explain: At the 'finca de café' a 'campesino' (farmer) shows them the coffee plants, so a 'finca' is a farm.
